OWBPA GROUP/EXIT-INCENTIVE PROGRAM DISCLOSURE NOTICE
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Corp.

GROUP/CLASS DISCLOSURE NOTICE
NOTICE REQUIRED FOR A WAIVER OFFERED IN CONNECTION WITH A GROUP PROGRAM

To: Jordan Lee
From: Acme Corp.
Date of this notice: September 4, 2026
Program: 2026 Voluntary Separation Program

This notice is provided because Acme Corp. is requesting a waiver of age-discrimination claims from Jordan Lee in connection with 2026 Voluntary Separation Program, an exit-incentive or other employment-termination program offered to a group or class of employees. It is given at the start of Jordan Lee's consideration period for that waiver, and is in addition to the release itself.

Class, unit, or group covered by the program: All Customer Support Representatives in the Sacramento office

Eligibility factors for the program: Employees in the decisional unit with 5 or more years of service as of the program date

Time limits applicable to the program: Election window open September 4, 2026 through October 19, 2026

The job titles and ages of individuals eligible or selected for the program, and the ages of individuals in the same job classification or organizational unit who are not eligible or selected, are set out below.

CLASS, ELIGIBILITY, AND TIME-LIMIT DISCLOSURE FOR GROUP WAIVERS
When Acme Corp. requests a waiver of age-discrimination claims from Jordan Lee in connection with an exit-incentive program or other employment-termination program offered to a group or class of employees, federal law imposes a disclosure duty on top of the individual waiver's own requirements. At the start of the consideration period, Acme Corp. must inform Jordan Lee in writing, in a manner calculated to be understood by the average individual eligible to participate, of any class, unit, or group of individuals covered by the program, any eligibility factors for the program, and any time limits applicable to the program. The required information must be given to each individual in the decisional unit who is asked to sign a waiver, and its stated purpose is to give that individual enough information to make an informed choice about signing.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "if a waiver is requested in connection with an exit incentive or other employment termination program offered to a group or class of employees, the employer (at the commencement of the period specified in subparagraph (F)) informs the individual in writing in a manner calculated to be understood by the average individual eligible to participate, as to— (i) any class, unit, or group of individuals covered by such program, any eligibility factors for such program, and any time limits applicable to such program;"
  — 29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H)(i) (Cornell LII text), U.S. Code, Older Workers Benefit Protection Act, group-program class/eligibility/time-limit disclosure (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/626)
  "The required information must be given to each person in the decisional unit who is asked to sign a waiver agreement."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(2) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, who must receive the disclosure (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  "The purpose of the informational requirements is to provide an employee with enough information regarding the program to allow the employee to make an informed choice whether or not to sign a waiver agreement."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(1)(iv) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, stated purpose of the disclosure (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  Known gap: The statutory quote below (29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H)(i)) is independently verified primary law. The two 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f) quotes are EEOC's own regulation interpreting that same statutory disclosure duty — they elaborate the rule rather than corroborate it from a second, independent source, and are treated that way here. This clause is meant to be used together with this corpus's Severance Agreement document: the individual-waiver requirements this group-disclosure duty sits on top of — the 21-day/45-day consideration period, 7-day revocation period, plain-language and attorney-consultation requirements, and the EEOC-participation carve-out — are covered there, in the clause titled "Age Discrimination Release Requirements" (clause id sev_owbpa), not here. This clause does not itself determine whether a specific severance or exit program in fact qualifies as an "exit incentive or other employment termination program offered to a group or class of employees" for purposes of triggering this disclosure duty, and does not define a specific employer's "decisional unit" — the regulation itself treats both as case-by-case, fact-dependent determinations.

DECISIONAL UNIT AND WHAT COUNTS AS A COVERED PROGRAM
EEOC regulations interpreting this disclosure duty explain that "class," "unit," "group," "job classification," and "organizational unit" are examples of categories of employees, and that regardless of which term applies, their scope in a given case is worked out by identifying the employer's "decisional unit" for the program at issue. The same regulations describe two types of programs the disclosure duty can attach to: an exit-incentive program, usually a voluntary program under which employees are offered additional consideration in exchange for resigning and signing a waiver, and another employment-termination program, usually one under which employees are involuntarily terminated and offered additional consideration for signing a waiver.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Regardless of the type of program, the scope of the terms “class,” “unit,” “group,” “job classification,” and “organizational unit” is determined by examining the “decisional unit” at issue."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(1)(iii)(C) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, scope of covered terms tied to the decisional unit (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  "Usually an “exit incentive program” is a voluntary program offered to a group or class of employees where such employees are offered consideration in addition to anything of value to which the individuals are already entitled (hereinafter in this section, “additional consideration”) in exchange for their decision to resign voluntarily and sign a waiver. Usually “other employment termination program” refers to a group or class of employees who were involuntarily terminated and who are offered additional consideration in return for their decision to sign a waiver."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(1)(iii)(A) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, exit-incentive programs versus other employment-termination programs (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  Known gap: Both citations below are subsections of the same regulatory section, 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(1)(iii) — they are treated as one source elaborating the statutory group-disclosure requirement in 29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H), not as independent corroboration of each other or of the statute. This clause is meant to be used together with this corpus's Severance Agreement document (clause id sev_owbpa), which covers the individual 21/45-day and 7-day requirements this group-disclosure duty does not restate. This clause does not determine whether a specific employer's specific program is in fact an "exit incentive or other employment termination program offered to a group or class of employees" that triggers the disclosure duty, and does not define a specific employer's decisional unit — the regulation itself says both are decided case-by-case on the specific facts, including the employer's own corporate structure.

JOB-TITLES-AND-AGES DISCLOSURE FOR THOSE SELECTED AND NOT SELECTED
The same group-program disclosure duty also requires Acme Corp. to inform Jordan Lee, in the same writing, of the job titles and ages of all individuals eligible or selected for the program, and the ages of all individuals in the same job classification or organizational unit who are not eligible or selected for the program. EEOC regulations implementing this requirement direct that ages be broken down individually — an age band such as "age 20-30" does not satisfy the requirement — and that if the individuals actually being terminated are only a subset of a larger decisional unit, the disclosure must still cover the entire decisional unit, not only the subset selected.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "the job titles and ages of all individuals eligible or selected for the program, and the ages of all individuals in the same job classification or organizational unit who are not eligible or selected for the program."
  — 29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H)(ii) (Cornell LII text), U.S. Code, Older Workers Benefit Protection Act, group-program job-title-and-age disclosure (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/626)
  "Information regarding ages should be broken down according to the age of each person eligible or selected for the program and each person not eligible or selected for the program. The use of age bands broader than one year (such as “age 20-30”) does not satisfy this requirement."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(4)(ii) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, ages must be disclosed individually, not in bands (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  "If the terminees are selected from a subset of a decisional unit, the employer must still disclose information for the entire population of the decisional unit."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(4)(v) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, disclosure must cover the whole decisional unit even if only a subset is terminated (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  Known gap: The statutory quote below (29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H)(ii)) is independently verified primary law. The two 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(4) quotes are EEOC's own regulation elaborating that same statutory requirement, not an independent second source, and are treated that way here. This clause is meant to be used together with this corpus's Severance Agreement document, in particular the clause titled "Age Discrimination Release Requirements" (clause id sev_owbpa), which covers the individual 21/45-day consideration period and 7-day revocation period this group disclosure does not restate. This clause does not reproduce every subpart of 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(4) — for example, its rules on breaking down grades or subcategories within a job title, on combined voluntary/involuntary terminations, and on successive-increment terminations are not covered here. This clause does not itself calculate any specific employer's ages, job titles, or decisional-unit population, and does not determine whether a specific disclosure an employer actually gave satisfied this requirement.

JOB TITLES AND AGES DISCLOSURE
AGES AND JOB TITLES — ELIGIBLE OR SELECTED, AND NOT ELIGIBLE OR SELECTED

Decisional unit: All Customer Support Representatives in the Sacramento office

Ages of individuals eligible or selected for 2026 Voluntary Separation Program, by job title:
Customer Support Representative: 34, 41, 47, 52, 58

Ages of individuals in the same job classification or organizational unit who are NOT eligible or selected for 2026 Voluntary Separation Program, by job title:
Customer Support Representative: 29, 33, 39

Ages above are listed individually for each person; they are not grouped into ranges or bands.

SCOPE OF THE DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENT ITSELF
The EEOC regulation implementing this disclosure duty states that its own reach is confined to what the disclosure statute requires: it is limited to the requirements of 29 U.S.C. § 626(f)(1)(H) and is not intended to affect the scope of discovery, or of substantive proceedings, in the processing or litigation of an age-discrimination charge.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This regulatory section is limited to the requirements of section 7(f)(1)(H) and is not intended to affect the scope of discovery or of substantive proceedings in the processing of charges of violation of the ADEA or in litigation involving such charges."
  — 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(3)(vii) (Cornell LII e-CFR text), Code of Federal Regulations, EEOC interpretive regulation, the disclosure rule's own limited scope (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1625.22)
  Known gap: This citation is to 29 C.F.R. § 1625.22(f)(3)(vii) alone — the EEOC's own limiting statement about the reach of its regulation — and is not paired with an independent statutory quote, since the statute itself does not address discovery or litigation scope. Making this disclosure, or complying with it, does not by itself resolve, settle, or waive any age-discrimination claim, and this clause does not state that it does; it states only that the regulation's disclosure rule does not expand or contract discovery or litigation scope beyond what the statute requires. This clause is meant to be used together with this corpus's Severance Agreement document (clause id sev_owbpa) for the individual waiver requirements — the 21/45-day consideration period, 7-day revocation period, and EEOC-participation carve-out — that this clause does not cover. This clause does not determine whether a specific disclosure a specific employer gave was adequate under the statute or regulation.
